text: Little Roy led his sheep down to pasture, And his cows, by the side of the brook;
Lucy very kindly took it up and threw it into the air, but, her brother neglecting to run off at the same moment, the kite fell down again.
Yes; she has a pan with some eggs in it.
The boys have come out on the porch to blow bubbles.
For the pasture was gay as a garden, And it glowed with a flowery red; But the meadows had never a grass blade, And the brooklet--it slept in its bed:

They did, and with more care; but a side wind coming suddenly, as Lucy let go the kite, it was blown against some shrubs, and the tail became entangled in a moment, leaving the poor kite hanging with its head downward.
